name: Wind Cold with Internal Heat
description: Wind Cold with Internal Heat (Fēng Hán Jiān Nèi Rè, 风寒兼内热) is a full TCM pattern. Key signs: Severe aversion to cold, High fever, Absence of sweating. Relate...
key_signs: ["Severe aversion to cold", "High fever", "Absence of sweating", "Generalised body aches and pains", "Headache", "Irritability and agitation", "Thirst or dry mouth", "Rapid and laboured breathing", "Cough with thick yellow phlegm", "Sore throat", "Chest tightness", "Nasal congestion with thick discharge", "Stiffness in the neck and upper back", "Difficulty sleeping due to restlessness", "Feeling of heat in the chest", "Red or painful eyes", "Dry nose", "Dark scanty urine", "Constipation", "Slight breathlessness", "Facial flushing", "Bitter taste in the mouth", "Wheezing"]
worse_with: ["Cold weather or exposure to wind", "Night-time", "Physical exertion", "Warm rooms that increase inner restlessness", "Lying down (worsens breathing difficulty)", "Eating spicy or greasy food"]
better_with: ["Gentle sweating that breaks through", "Warm drinks in small sips", "Rest in a moderately warm environment", "Cool compress on the forehead"]
timing_worsening_explanation: Symptoms often develop acutely, within hours of exposure to cold wind. The chills and body aches tend to be worst in the initial stage, while the internal Heat signs (irritability, thirst, sore throat) may intensify as the day progresses. Fever typically peaks in the afternoon or evening. If untreated, the exterior Cold layer may resolve within a few days, but the interior Heat can deepen and transform into a full interior Heat pattern.
practitioner_notes:
The key to diagnosing this pattern lies in recognising two seemingly contradictory sets of symptoms occurring simultaneously. On one hand, there are clear signs of an outer invasion by Cold: strong chills, body aches, stiff neck, headache, and an absolute absence of sweating. On the other hand, there are unmistakable signs of Heat: irritability, agitation, thirst, a red tongue tip, and a rapid pulse. This combination is the hallmark of the pattern.
The diagnostic reasoning follows a classical principle: when Wind-Cold tightly locks the body's surface, it prevents the normal release of Heat through the pores. If a person already has some internal Heat (perhaps from a naturally warm constitution, emotional stress, rich diet, or a pre-existing mild Heat condition), that Heat becomes trapped and intensifies. Alternatively, severe Cold exposure can itself generate Heat as the body's defensive Qi fights the invader vigorously. The classical metaphor is 'Cold wrapping Fire' (寒包火 Hán Bāo Huǒ), meaning the Cold acts like a lid on a pot, trapping the fire within.
The tongue and pulse are especially important for confirmation. A floating and tight pulse confirms exterior Cold, while rapidity confirms interior Heat. A tongue with a mixed white-and-yellow coating, or a red body with a white coat and red tip, captures both the Cold and Heat aspects. The presence of both strong chills (which suggest Cold) and marked irritability or agitation (which suggest Heat) in the same person is the most reliable clinical pointer, since pure Cold patterns produce lethargy rather than agitation, and pure Heat patterns produce aversion to heat rather than strong chills.
pathophysiology: Wind-Cold locks the body's surface shut, trapping pre-existing or developing Heat inside and creating a pattern where the person is simultaneously cold on the outside and hot on the inside.
treatment_principle: Release the exterior to dispel Wind-Cold while simultaneously clearing internal Heat
typical_timeline: 3-7 days for uncomplicated cases with prompt herbal treatment; 1-2 weeks if treatment is delayed or complications develop
formula_modifications:
If irritability and thirst are very pronounced (strong internal Heat): Increase the dosage of Shi Gao (Gypsum) and consider adding Tian Hua Fen (Trichosanthes Root) to clear Heat and generate fluids.
If there is a sore or swollen throat: Add Jin Yin Hua (Honeysuckle), Lian Qiao (Forsythia), and Niu Bang Zi (Arctium) to clear Heat-toxin from the throat.
If coughing and wheezing are prominent: Increase Xing Ren (Apricot Seed) dosage and add Ban Xia (Pinellia), Su Zi (Perilla Seed), and Sang Bai Pi (Mulberry Root Bark) to descend Lung Qi and relieve wheezing.
If the person also has puffy swelling in the face and limbs (fluid accumulation): Add Fu Ling (Poria), Zhu Ling (Polyporus), and Ting Li Zi (Lepidium) to promote urination and reduce swelling.
If the external Cold symptoms are mild (less chills, less body ache): Reduce Ma Huang dosage to prevent excessive sweating. One may shift toward Ma Xing Shi Gan Tang, which is gentler on exterior-releasing while still clearing Lung Heat.
If there is also loss of appetite or nausea: Add Sheng Jiang (Fresh Ginger) and Ban Xia to harmonise the Stomach and stop nausea.

formulas.name: Da Qing Long Tang
formulas.description: The signature formula for this pattern. From the Shang Han Lun, Da Qing Long Tang (Major Bluegreen Dragon Decoction) uses heavy Ma Huang with Shi Gao to simultaneously release strong exterior Wind-Cold and clear interior Heat. Its cardinal indications are severe chills, fever, body pain, absence of sweating, and irritability.

formulas.name: Ma Xing Shi Gan Tang
formulas.description: Ma Xing Shi Gan Tang (Ephedra, Apricot Seed, Gypsum, and Licorice Decoction) is used when the exterior Cold has partly resolved but Heat has entered the Lungs, causing coughing, wheezing, fever, and thirst. Lighter on exterior-releasing than Da Qing Long Tang and heavier on clearing Lung Heat.

formulas.name: Chai Ge Jie Ji Tang
formulas.description: Chai Ge Jie Ji Tang (Bupleurum and Kudzu Decoction to Release the Muscle Layer) treats Wind-Cold that has begun transforming into Heat and spreading to all three Yang channels. Used when chills are lessening but fever is intensifying, with symptoms like eye pain, dry nose, insomnia, and dry throat.

herbs.name: Ma Huang
herbs.description: The chief herb for this pattern. Ma Huang (Ephedra) powerfully opens the pores and induces sweating to expel Wind-Cold from the exterior. Used in heavy dosage in Da Qing Long Tang to match the severity of exterior Cold constraint.

herbs.name: Shi Gao
herbs.description: Shi Gao (Gypsum) is acrid and very cold, clearing interior Heat and relieving irritability. Paired with Ma Huang, it clears Heat from inside while Ma Huang releases Cold from outside, achieving simultaneous interior-exterior treatment.

herbs.name: Gui Zhi
herbs.description: Gui Zhi (Cinnamon Twig) assists Ma Huang in releasing the exterior and warming the channels. It helps open the surface and push the pathogen outward.

herbs.name: Xing Ren
herbs.description: Xing Ren (Bitter Apricot Seed) descends Lung Qi and relieves coughing and wheezing. It pairs with Ma Huang to restore the Lung's natural function of dispersing and descending.

herbs.name: Huang Qin
herbs.description: Huang Qin (Scutellaria) clears Heat from the Lungs and upper body. Used when the internal Heat component is prominent and affects the Lung or Shaoyang level.

herbs.name: Ge Gen
herbs.description: Ge Gen (Kudzu Root) releases the muscle layer and generates fluids. Especially useful when the pattern involves the Yangming channel with stiff neck and strong Heat.

herbs.name: Chai Hu
herbs.description: Chai Hu (Bupleurum) vents Heat from the interior through the exterior. It is key in formulas like Chai Ge Jie Ji Tang where the Cold has partly transformed into Heat affecting Shaoyang.

herbs.name: Dan Dou Chi
herbs.description: Dan Dou Chi (Fermented Soybean) gently releases the exterior and vents pent-up Heat. It works well in milder presentations of this pattern.

acupoints.name: Lieque LU-7
acupoints.description: Command point of the head and neck, opens and disperses Lung Qi. Used with reducing method to release the exterior and restore the Lung's dispersing function.

acupoints.name: Hegu LI-4
acupoints.description: The most important point for expelling exterior Wind. Releases the exterior, opens the pores, clears Heat from the Yangming channel. Needled with reducing method.

acupoints.name: Fengchi GB-20
acupoints.description: Expels Wind from the head and neck, relieves headache and stiff neck. Benefits the eyes and clears the head. Needled with reducing method directed toward the opposite eye.

acupoints.name: Dazhui DU-14
acupoints.description: Meeting point of all six Yang channels and the Du Mai. Clears Heat, releases the exterior, and reduces fever. Especially effective for clearing Heat in exterior conditions.

acupoints.name: Quchi LI-11
acupoints.description: Clears Heat and cools the Blood. He-Sea point of the Large Intestine channel, effective for reducing fever and clearing interior Heat from the Yangming.

acupoints.name: Chize LU-5
acupoints.description: He-Sea point of the Lung channel, clears Lung Heat and descends rebellious Qi. Useful when the internal Heat component causes coughing and chest congestion.

acupoints.name: Feishu BL-13
acupoints.description: Back-Shu point of the Lung. Regulates Lung Qi, releases the exterior, and clears Lung Heat. Cupping on this point is particularly effective for releasing exterior pathogens.

faqs.question: What is Wind Cold with Internal Heat in TCM?
faqs.answer: Wind-Cold locks the body's surface shut, trapping pre-existing or developing Heat inside and creating a pattern where the person is simultaneously cold on the outside and hot on the inside.

faqs.question: What are the key signs of Wind Cold with Internal Heat?
faqs.answer: Key signs include: Severe aversion to cold, High fever, Absence of sweating, Generalised body aches and pains, Headache, Irritability and agitation, Thirst or dry mouth, Rapid and laboured breathing, Cough with thick yellow phlegm, Sore throat, Chest tightness, Nasal congestion with thick discharge.

faqs.question: What formulas treat Wind Cold with Internal Heat?
faqs.answer: Common formulas for Wind Cold with Internal Heat include: Da Qing Long Tang, Ma Xing Shi Gan Tang, Chai Ge Jie Ji Tang.

faqs.question: What Western conditions relate to Wind Cold with Internal Heat?
faqs.answer: This pattern is associated with: Influenza, Upper respiratory tract infection, Acute bronchitis, Pneumonia, Acute tonsillitis, Urticaria (cold-induced with Heat signs), Acute nephritis.

faqs.question: What is the treatment principle for Wind Cold with Internal Heat?
faqs.answer: Release the exterior to dispel Wind-Cold while simultaneously clearing internal Heat
